note: A soldierless species; the worker and the enteric valve (EVA) are the main diagnostic basis. It was previously recorded from Ecuador as Anoplotermes grp AC and from French Guiana as Anoplotermes-group sp. AK. The specific name honours Susan G. Scheffrahn, wife of R. H. Scheffrahn.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The enteric valve bears a 'stellate' sclerotised plate on only one of the valve pads, which distinguishes it from all other species of Anoplotermes; all the pads bear longitudinal ridges. The mixed segment has an inflated mesenteric tongue. It differs from A. parvus, which also has a sclerotised plate on the enteric valve, but in that species the plate forms an asymmetrical multispinose mass. In the phylogenetic analysis this species is the sister group of the other four Anoplotermes included in that study (including the type species); the enteric valve and COI sequences alone once suggested that it should be placed in a separate genus, but the external morphology, the gut morphology and the complete mitochondrial genome support keeping it in Anoplotermes. Distribution: Ecuador, Brazil, French Guiana; mostly collected in surface and small epigeal nests, and once recorded adjacent to workers of Anhangatermes.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text:
Very small. Head capsule pale red, covered with numerous short hairs and a few sparse setae. Eyes oval, the dorsoventral diameter shorter. Ocelli round, relatively large compared with the eyes. Fontanelle oval, very small. Postclypeus hardly inflated, pale brown, concolorous with the meso- and metanotal plates. Anteclypeus narrow, anterolateral margins slightly concave, apex rounded. Antenna 12-segmented (segment-length formula 2>3≈4<5). Pronotum with short setae on the margins and very short hairs on the surface; anterior margin straight, concave in the middle. Mesonotum and metanotum covered with numerous short hairs.

Alate measurements (2 nests, 3 females; 1 nest, 1 male, mm): head length (to the lateral base of the mandibles) 0.41—0.43 (male 0.37); maximum head width 0.42—0.44 (male 0.42); interocular distance 0.40—0.41 (male 0.40); maximum diameter of the ocellus 0.07—0.08 (male 0.07); minimum diameter of the ocellus 0.05—0.06 (male 0.05); maximum diameter of the eye 0.19—0.20 (male 0.17); minimum diameter of the eye 0.15—0.17 (male 0.15); pronotum length 0.27—0.30 (male 0.27); pronotum width 0.41—0.45 (male 0.42); hind tibia length 0.45—0.47 (male 0.37); fore tibia length 0.37—0.37 (male 0.37); fore tibia width 0.06—0.07 (male 0.07).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text:
Monomorphic. Very small. Head capsule and antennal segments almost white. Fontanelle indistinct. Antenna 12- or 13-segmented. Postclypeus moderately inflated. Head capsule covered with numerous short hairs, with additional sparse long setae on the anteclypeus and the postclypeus. Left mandible: apical tooth more prominent than M1+2, the notch between the two acute; posterior margin of M1+2 slightly concave; third marginal tooth (M3) less prominent than M1+2, its two margins forming an acute angle; molar projection well developed, concealing the molar tooth in dorsal view. Right mandible: apical tooth more prominent than M1; the notch between M1 and M2 a right angle; posterior margin of M2 concave. Pronotum with both long setae and short hairs on the margins and the surface. Tergites and sternites with short hairs and microtrichia on the margins and the surface. Fore tibia strongly inflated and short; the inner surface with a row of long setae from the middle to the apex.

Gut: elongate; the mesenteric tongue of the mixed segment with a white globular mesenteric nodule in ventral view. First proctodeal segment (P1) of uniform width throughout its length. Enteric valve seating (EVS) slender, cylindrical; a 'stellate' sclerotised plate on only one valve pad, the margin of the plate bearing 16—20 spines, with a further 1—3 spines on the plate surface. Pads and interpad areas with longitudinal ridges; the proximal part of the pads smooth and unornamented (and therefore crepe-like, very commonly so); the distal part of the pads with 5—7 short, posteriorly directed spines on the inflated central part of the pad. The enteric valve seating is filled with bacteria on 'bacterial mucus'.

Worker measurements (3 nests, 10 individuals, mm, range/mean): head length (to the lateral base of the mandibles) 0.26—0.41/0.35; maximum head width 0.43—0.60/0.50; hind tibia length 0.30—0.46/0.36; fore tibia length 0.29—0.40/0.33; fore tibia width 0.09—0.14/0.10; fore tibia width/length ratio 0.22—0.38/0.32.
